desk_read: Energy led the selling yesterday: Natural Gas dropped -3.11% on below-average volume with long liquidation draining -12.2k contracts from total open interest, the sharpest net outflow in the complex and a sign that longs are exiting into weakness rather than being replaced. WTI echoed that tone, price -0.73% with total open interest -4.0k, also flagged as long liquidation, while Brent told a different story — price nearly as weak at -0.69% yet total open interest rose +1.5k, pointing to new shorts building. That Brent divergence, price down but open interest up on the short side, is where positioning looks most fragile to a snap-back. On the equity side, S&P 500 attracted new longs on above-average volume even as Nasdaq slipped, a quiet split worth watching.
oil_read: WTI slipped 0.73% on long liquidation, with total open interest off 4.0k contracts (-0.4%) and volume running at only 0.9x its 20-day average, signalling a fragile, thinly committed bid. Brent edged down 0.69% but attracted new shorts, total open interest rising 1.5k contracts (+1.2%) on volume of 0.8x average. Both curves remain in backwardation, with WTI's CLX26-CLJ27 spread at +9.78 $/bbl and Brent's BZZ26-BZK27 at +13.62 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI is neutral, with long liquidation and a narrowing backwardation spread warning of exhaustion rather than supporting any directional move. Brent is also neutral, but fresh shorts entering into a steepening backwardation structure warn of crowding risk on the downside and a potential short squeeze if the curve firms. Copper's mildly bullish bias, built on new longs, supports continuation of the current move with a more durable foundation. S&P 500 is likewise mildly bullish, with fresh positioning that supports the prevailing trend rather than flagging exhaustion. Across markets, the overall picture is cautious: energy positioning looks fragile, while Copper and S&P 500 offer the clearest, most durable bullish tilt of the session.
